Counterfactual joint distribution of the two responses

Source: R/probability.R
cf_prob.Rd

Computes \(P\{Y_{1,k}(a_1, a_2) = y_1, Y_{2,k}(a_1, a_2) = y_2 \mid X = x\}\), the joint distribution of the two responses at visit \(k\) had the treatment components been set to \((a_1, a_2)\), through the recursive formula of Theorems 2 and 3 of the paper, from the fitted (or given) models. The combinations \((1, 0)\) and \((0, 1)\) are counterfactual: they are identified under the conditions of the paper.

Usage

cf_prob(object, newdata = NULL, a1, a2, K = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted model returned by biscal().

newdata

A data frame of covariate values, one row per covariate profile \(x\). May be omitted when the model has no covariates.

a1, a2

Values (0 or 1) of the treatment components acting on the first and the second response.

K

Visit(s) \(k\) at which the distribution is computed; defaults to the last visit of the data. 0 gives the baseline distribution. Visits after the last visit of the data are extrapolated with the fitted transition models (with a warning).

Value

An array with dimensions (profile, category of the first response, category of the second response, visit), with dimnames.

References

Hu, P. and Yi, G. Y. (2026). Inference about separable causal effects with longitudinal bivariate ordinal responses with missingness and censoring. Statistics in Medicine, 45, e70320. doi:10.1002/sim.70320

See also

gor() for the generalized odds ratios.

Examples

fit <- biscal(cbind(y1, y2) ~ x1 + x2, data = simtrial, id = "id",
              time = "visit", treatment = "trt")
pr <- cf_prob(fit, newdata = data.frame(x1 = 0, x2 = 1), a1 = 1, a2 = 0)
pr[1, , , 1]          # joint distribution at the last visit
#>    y2
#> y1           0          1
#>   0 0.02200795 0.03601437
#>   1 0.14134513 0.80063255
sum(pr[1, , , 1])     # sums to one
#> [1] 1
